candidates.computation_change_reason: Parameter name and CAS number govern matching to facility discharge points and reported measurements; a different identification (e.g., total vs dissolved manganese, or CAS mismatch) would change which limit and monitoring obligation rows are evaluated.

If interpreted as an enforceable numeric discharge limit for this parameter rather than a non-limit column value (e.g., background, detection level, or study statistic), the applicable limit and exceedance determination for matching measurements would change.

This value appears multiple times in the row; depending on which table column each occurrence represents (e.g., monthly, seasonal, or annual limit), a different column-to-period mapping would change which enforceable limit applies to each monitoring period.

If read as a sentinel indicating no numeric limit or non-enforceable placeholder rather than a literal concentration, numeric compliance comparison may be inapplicable; alternatively, if treated as a real limit, exceedance analysis would differ and missing-evidence cases would be classified differently.

These distinct numeric values may represent calculated reasonable-potential projections, alternate limit bases, or period-specific limits; treating them as enforceable discharge limits versus analytical outputs would change which limit is applied and whether reported values exceed it.

N/A may indicate no enforceable numeric limit, report-only monitoring, monitoring not required, or a documented no-data state; each reading changes whether a limit comparison applies (A), whether monitoring was obligated (B), and how absent results are classified (C).
